ramayana-1-8-20.translation: 'After thinking, they will propose suitable means: "We will bring the Brahmin, and there will be no fault."
ramayana-1-8-20.meaning: They will find a clever way.
ramayana-1-8-20.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 8: childless Dasharatha plans a horse sacrifice, and Sumantra recalls an old prophecy about the sage Rishyashringa.

ramayana-1-8-21.translation: 'So by the lord of Anga, with courtesans, the sage's son was brought; the god rained, and Shanta was given to him.
ramayana-1-8-21.meaning: Rishyashringa came, rain fell and he married Shanta.
ramayana-1-8-21.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 8: childless Dasharatha plans a horse sacrifice, and Sumantra recalls an old prophecy about the sage Rishyashringa.

ramayana-1-8-22.translation: 'Rishyashringa, your son-in-law, will bring about your sons.' This is what Sanatkumara said, which I have told you.
ramayana-1-8-22.meaning: Rishyashringa will help Dasharatha have sons.
ramayana-1-8-22.explanation: Shanta is traditionally Dasharatha's daughter given to Lomapada; so Rishyashringa is his son-in-law.

ramayana-1-8-23.translation: Delighted, Dasharatha said to Sumantra: 'Tell me in detail how Rishyashringa was brought.'
ramayana-1-8-23.meaning: Dasharatha asked for the full story.
ramayana-1-8-23.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 8: childless Dasharatha plans a horse sacrifice, and Sumantra recalls an old prophecy about the sage Rishyashringa.

ramayana-1-9-1.translation: Urged by the king, Sumantra said: 'Hear with your ministers how Rishyashringa was brought.
ramayana-1-9-1.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-2.translation: 'The priest and ministers said to Lomapada: "We have thought of a safe plan.
ramayana-1-9-2.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-3.translation: '"Rishyashringa lives in the forest, devoted to austerity and study. He knows nothing of women, of the pleasures of the senses or of comfort.
ramayana-1-9-3.meaning: He knows nothing of the world.
ramayana-1-9-3.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-4.translation: '"We will bring him to the city with pleasing things that delight the senses and stir men's hearts. Let it be decided quickly."
ramayana-1-9-4.meaning: They planned to tempt him with pleasures.
ramayana-1-9-4.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-5.translation: '"Let beautiful, well-adorned courtesans go there. Tempting him by various means, they will bring him here, and they will be rewarded."
ramayana-1-9-5.meaning: They would send courtesans to lure him.
ramayana-1-9-5.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-6.translation: 'Hearing this, the king said "So be it" to the priest, and the priest and ministers did so.
ramayana-1-9-6.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-7.translation: 'Hearing this, the chief courtesans entered the great forest and tried to be seen near the hermitage by the stern sage's son, who always stayed there.
ramayana-1-9-7.meaning: The women went to the forest near his hermitage.
ramayana-1-9-7.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-8.translation: 'He was always content with his father and never went beyond the hermitage.
ramayana-1-9-8.meaning: Rishyashringa never left his father's hermitage.
ramayana-1-9-8.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-9.translation: 'Since his birth the ascetic had never seen a woman, or a man, or any other being from a city or kingdom.
ramayana-1-9-9.meaning: He had never seen anyone from the outside world.
ramayana-1-9-9.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-10.translation: 'Then one day, by chance, Vibhandaka's son came to that place and saw those lovely women.
ramayana-1-9-10.meaning: One day he came upon the women.
ramayana-1-9-10.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-11.translation: 'The women, in bright clothes, singing sweetly, approached the sage's son and all said:
ramayana-1-9-11.meaning: The women greeted him with song.
ramayana-1-9-11.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-12.translation: '"Who are you, Brahmin? How do you live? We want to know. Tell us why you wander alone in this lonely, fearsome forest."
ramayana-1-9-12.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-13.translation: 'Seeing for the first time these women of charming form in the forest, he felt affection and wanted to tell them of his father.
ramayana-1-9-13.meaning: Charmed, he told them about himself.
ramayana-1-9-13.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-14.translation: '"My father is Vibhandaka; I am his own son. My name, known on earth, is Rishyashringa, and so is my work.
ramayana-1-9-14.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-15.translation: '"Our hermitage is near here, lovely ones. I will honour all of you there with due rites."
ramayana-1-9-15.meaning: He invited them to his hermitage.
ramayana-1-9-15.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-16.translation: 'Hearing the sage's son, they all agreed and went with him to see the hermitage.
ramayana-1-9-16.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-17.translation: 'When they arrived, the sage's son honoured them: "Here is a guest offering, here water for your feet, here are our roots and fruits."
ramayana-1-9-17.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-18.translation: 'Accepting this, they were all eager but, fearing the sage, quickly decided to leave.
ramayana-1-9-18.meaning: They feared his father would return.
ramayana-1-9-18.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-19.translation: '"Brahmin, here are our own special fruits. Take them, bless you, and eat them without delay."
ramayana-1-9-19.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-20.translation: 'Then, joyfully embracing him, they gave him sweets and many kinds of good food.
ramayana-1-9-20.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-21.translation: 'Tasting them, the radiant youth thought they were fruits, never having tasted such things while living in the forest.
ramayana-1-9-21.meaning: He thought the sweets were fruits.

ramayana-1-9-22.translation: 'Taking leave of the Brahmin, saying they had a vow to keep, the women went away on that pretext, afraid of his father.
ramayana-1-9-22.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-23.translation: 'When they had all gone, Kashyapa's grandson was uneasy in his heart and felt sad.
ramayana-1-9-23.meaning: He felt restless after they left.
ramayana-1-9-23.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-24.translation: 'The next day the strong youth came again to the place where he had seen those charming, well-adorned women.
ramayana-1-9-24.meaning: He went back to find them.
ramayana-1-9-24.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-25.translation: 'Seeing the Brahmin coming, they were delighted, approached him and said:
ramayana-1-9-25.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-26.translation: '"Come to our hermitage, gentle one. There the rites of hospitality will be even finer."
ramayana-1-9-26.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-27.translation: 'Hearing their heart-touching words, he decided to go, and the women led him away.
ramayana-1-9-27.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-28.translation: 'As that great Brahmin was being brought, the god suddenly rained, delighting the world.
ramayana-1-9-28.meaning: Rain fell as soon as he came.
ramayana-1-9-28.explanation: His mere arrival ends the drought.

ramayana-1-9-29.translation: 'As the sage arrived with the rain in his kingdom, the king went out to meet him and bowed, touching the ground with his head.
ramayana-1-9-29.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-30.translation: 'With full attention he offered him the guest offering properly, and asked the great Brahmin for grace, so that anger would not enter him.
ramayana-1-9-30.meaning: The king asked the sage not to be angry.
ramayana-1-9-30.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-31.translation: 'Entering the inner palace, the king gave him his daughter Shanta in marriage with due rites, and with a peaceful mind he was glad.
ramayana-1-9-31.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-9-32.translation: 'So the mighty Rishyashringa lived there with his wife Shanta, honoured with every comfort.'
ramayana-1-9-32.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 9: Sumantra tells how the forest-bred sage Rishyashringa was brought to the kingdom of Anga and ended a drought.

ramayana-1-10-1.translation: 'Hear more of my helpful words, great king, as that best of gods told them in the story:
ramayana-1-10-1.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-2.translation: '"In the Ikshvaku line will be born a very righteous king named Dasharatha, glorious and true to his promises.
ramayana-1-10-2.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-3.translation: '"That king will be friends with the king of Anga, who will have a fortunate daughter named Shanta.
ramayana-1-10-3.meaning: Dasharatha will be friends with Anga's king.
ramayana-1-10-3.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-4.translation: '"The son of the king of Anga will be known as Lomapada. Glorious Dasharatha will go to him and say:
ramayana-1-10-4.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-5.translation: '"Righteous one, I have no children. Let Shanta's husband, at your command, perform my sacrifice for the continuance of my line."
ramayana-1-10-5.meaning: Dasharatha will ask for Rishyashringa's help.
ramayana-1-10-5.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-6.translation: '"Hearing this and thinking it over, the self-possessed king will send Shanta's husband, who can bring sons.
ramayana-1-10-6.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-7.translation: '"Receiving the Brahmin, the king, free of worry, will perform that sacrifice with a joyful heart.
ramayana-1-10-7.meaning: Dasharatha will hold the sacrifice joyfully.
ramayana-1-10-7.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-8.translation: '"King Dasharatha, wishing to sacrifice, will with folded hands choose Rishyashringa, best of Brahmins.
ramayana-1-10-8.meaning: He will ask Rishyashringa to lead it.
ramayana-1-10-8.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-9.translation: '"For the sacrifice, for offspring and for heaven, the lord of men will gain his wish from that chief of Brahmins.
ramayana-1-10-9.meaning: He will get what he wants.
ramayana-1-10-9.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-10.translation: '"He will have four sons of boundless valour, who will establish the line and be famous in all the worlds."
ramayana-1-10-10.meaning: Four great sons will be born.
ramayana-1-10-10.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-11.translation: 'So the holy Sanatkumara, best of gods, told this story long ago, in the age of the gods.
ramayana-1-10-11.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-12.translation: 'So, tiger among men, great king, go yourself with your army and vehicles and bring him with honour.'
ramayana-1-10-12.meaning: Sumantra urged the king to go in person.
ramayana-1-10-12.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-13.translation: With Vasishtha's leave, having heard the charioteer's words, the king set out with his queens and ministers to where the Brahmin was.
ramayana-1-10-13.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-14.translation: Crossing forests and rivers slowly, he came to the land where the great sage lived.
ramayana-1-10-14.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-15.translation: Reaching that best of Brahmins near Lomapada, he first saw the sage's son, blazing like fire.
ramayana-1-10-15.meaning: He saw Rishyashringa, glowing like fire.
ramayana-1-10-15.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-16.translation: Then the king honoured him duly and especially, out of friendship with Lomapada, with a joyful heart.
ramayana-1-10-16.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-17.translation: Lomapada told the wise sage's son of the friendship and the family tie, and he honoured the king in return.
ramayana-1-10-17.meaning: The friendship was explained to the sage.
ramayana-1-10-17.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-18.translation: Well honoured, the bull among men stayed with Lomapada seven or eight days, then said to the king:
ramayana-1-10-18.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-19.translation: 'King, let your daughter Shanta and her husband come to my city, for a great task is at hand.'
ramayana-1-10-19.meaning: He asked for Shanta and her husband to come to Ayodhya.
ramayana-1-10-19.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-20.translation: The king agreed to the wise sage going, and said to the Brahmin: 'Go with your wife.'
ramayana-1-10-20.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-21.translation: The sage's son agreed and said 'So be it' to the king; with the king's leave he set off with his wife.
ramayana-1-10-21.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-22.translation: Dasharatha and mighty Lomapada folded their hands to each other, embraced with affection, and rejoiced.
ramayana-1-10-22.meaning: The two kings embraced as friends.
ramayana-1-10-22.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-23.translation: Taking leave of his friend, the joy of the Raghus set out and sent swift messengers to the citizens: 'Have the whole city decorated at once.'
ramayana-1-10-23.meaning: Dasharatha sent word to decorate Ayodhya.
ramayana-1-10-23.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-24.translation: The delighted citizens, hearing the king was coming, did everything he had ordered.
ramayana-1-10-24.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-25.translation: Then the king entered the decorated city to the sound of conches and drums, with the bull among Brahmins in front.
ramayana-1-10-25.meaning: The king entered Ayodhya with great fanfare.
ramayana-1-10-25.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-26.translation: All the townspeople rejoiced to see the Brahmin being honoured and brought in by the king, whose deeds were like Indra's.
ramayana-1-10-26.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-27.translation: Bringing him into the inner palace and honouring him as the scriptures direct, the king felt his task was done by bringing him.
ramayana-1-10-27.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-28.translation: All the women of the palace, seeing large-eyed Shanta arrive with her husband, were filled with love and joy.
ramayana-1-10-28.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-10-29.translation: Honoured by them and especially by the king, she lived there happily for some time with the Brahmin.
ramayana-1-10-29.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 10: Sumantra finishes the prophecy, and Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa and Shanta to Ayodhya.

ramayana-1-11-1.translation: After a long time, when lovely spring had come, the king decided to sacrifice.
ramayana-1-11-1.meaning: In spring, the king resolved to hold the sacrifice.
ramayana-1-11-1.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-2.translation: Bowing his head to win the favour of the godlike Brahmin, he chose him for the sacrifice to continue his line.
ramayana-1-11-2.meaning: He asked Rishyashringa to lead it.
ramayana-1-11-2.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-3.translation: Well honoured, he said to the king: 'So be it. Let the materials be gathered and the horse released.'
ramayana-1-11-3.explanation: In the horse sacrifice, a horse wanders freely for a year before the rite.

ramayana-1-11-4.translation: Then the king said to Sumantra, best of ministers: 'Sumantra, quickly summon the priests who know the Vedas.'
ramayana-1-11-4.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-5.translation: Sumantra went swiftly and brought all those Brahmins, masters of the Vedas:
ramayana-1-11-5.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-6.translation: Suyajna, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kashyapa, the family priest Vasishtha and other excellent Brahmins.
ramayana-1-11-6.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-7.translation: Honouring them, righteous King Dasharatha spoke gentle words full of dharma and purpose:
ramayana-1-11-7.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-8.translation: 'I have no happiness, longing for a son. So I have decided to perform the horse sacrifice.
ramayana-1-11-8.meaning: He explained his grief and plan.
ramayana-1-11-8.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-9.translation: 'I wish to sacrifice by the rite the scriptures teach, and by the power of the sage's son I will gain my desires.'
ramayana-1-11-9.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-10.translation: The Brahmins led by Vasishtha praised the king's words, saying 'Excellent!'
ramayana-1-11-10.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-11.translation: Led by Rishyashringa, they replied: 'Let the materials be gathered and the horse released.
ramayana-1-11-11.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-12.translation: 'You will surely gain four sons of boundless valour, since your righteous mind has turned to this for sons.'
ramayana-1-11-12.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-13.translation: The king was pleased hearing the Brahmins, and joyfully told his ministers these auspicious words:
ramayana-1-11-13.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-14.translation: 'At my teachers' word, let the materials be gathered quickly, and let the horse be released, guarded by able men and with a priest.'
ramayana-1-11-14.meaning: Gather everything and release the horse.
ramayana-1-11-14.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-15.translation: 'Let the sacrificial ground be prepared on the north bank of the Sarayu, and let peace rites be increased as prescribed.'
ramayana-1-11-15.meaning: Prepare the ground by the Sarayu.
ramayana-1-11-15.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-16.translation: 'Any king can perform this sacrifice, provided no serious error occurs in this best of rites.'
ramayana-1-11-16.meaning: The rite must be done without mistakes.
ramayana-1-11-16.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-17.translation: 'Learned brahmarakshasas look for flaws here; one who sacrifices without proper rules is destroyed at once.'
ramayana-1-11-17.meaning: Errors in the rite are dangerous.
ramayana-1-11-17.explanation: Ancient belief held that mistakes in ritual invited harm.

ramayana-1-11-18.translation: 'So let arrangements be made so that my sacrifice is completed properly; you are capable in these matters.'
ramayana-1-11-18.meaning: Make sure it is done right.
ramayana-1-11-18.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-19.translation: All the ministers agreed and did as the king commanded.
ramayana-1-11-19.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-20.translation: The Brahmins praised the righteous king and, with his leave, went back the way they had come.
ramayana-1-11-20.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-11-21.translation: When the Brahmins had gone, the radiant king dismissed his ministers and entered his own palace.
ramayana-1-11-21.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 11: Dasharatha asks Rishyashringa and the priests to begin the horse sacrifice for sons.

ramayana-1-12-1.translation: When spring came again a full year had passed. Greeting Vasishtha and honouring him duly,
ramayana-1-12-1.meaning: A year later, the king approached Vasishtha.
ramayana-1-12-1.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-2.translation: he said humbly to that best of Brahmins, for the sake of offspring: 'Brahmin, best of sages, let my sacrifice be performed as prescribed.
ramayana-1-12-2.meaning: He asked Vasishtha to conduct the sacrifice.
ramayana-1-12-2.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-3.translation: 'Arrange it so no obstacle arises in any part of the sacrifice. You are my affectionate friend and my great teacher.
ramayana-1-12-3.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-4.translation: 'You must bear the burden of this sacrifice.' 'So be it,' said that best of Brahmins to the king.
ramayana-1-12-4.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-5.translation: 'I will do all you have asked.' Then he spoke to the elderly Brahmins skilled in sacrificial work,
ramayana-1-12-5.meaning: Vasishtha gave orders to the experts.
ramayana-1-12-5.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-6.translation: to the old and very righteous experts in building, to overseers, craftsmen, carpenters and diggers,
ramayana-1-12-6.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-7.translation: to accountants and artisans, actors and dancers, and to pure, learned men well versed in the scriptures:
ramayana-1-12-7.meaning: He called all kinds of skilled people.
ramayana-1-12-7.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-8.translation: 'By the king's command, begin the work of the sacrifice. Bring many thousands of bricks quickly.
ramayana-1-12-8.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-9.translation: 'Build fine lodgings for the kings, with every comfort, and hundreds of good houses for the Brahmins,
ramayana-1-12-9.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-10.translation: 'well stocked with plenty of food and drink. Also build spacious lodgings for the citizens,
ramayana-1-12-10.meaning: Provide food and lodging for all.
ramayana-1-12-10.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-11.translation: 'with lots of food and every comfort. And for the country people too, very fine ones.
ramayana-1-12-11.meaning: Care for country people as well.
ramayana-1-12-11.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-12.translation: 'Give food properly and with respect, not carelessly, so that all classes receive honour and are well treated.
ramayana-1-12-12.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-13.translation: 'Do not show disrespect even out of desire or anger. The workers and craftsmen who labour steadily at the sacrifice
ramayana-1-12-13.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-14.translation: 'should be honoured especially, in due order, so that everything is well done and nothing is neglected.
ramayana-1-12-14.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-15.translation: 'Do all this with loving hearts.' Then they all came together and said to Vasishtha:
ramayana-1-12-15.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-16.translation: 'We will do as you say; nothing will be neglected.' Then Vasishtha called Sumantra and said:
ramayana-1-12-16.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-17.translation: 'Invite the righteous kings of the earth, and thousands of Brahmins, warriors, merchants and labourers.
ramayana-1-12-17.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-18.translation: 'Bring people from every land with honour, and the brave Janaka, lord of Mithila, true in valour,
ramayana-1-12-18.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-19.translation: 'learned in all the sciences and the Vedas. Bring that fortunate man yourself with honour. Knowing him to be an old relation, I mention him first.
ramayana-1-12-19.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-20.translation: 'Likewise bring yourself the king of Kashi, affectionate and always kind-spoken, of good conduct and like a god.
ramayana-1-12-20.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-21.translation: 'Bring here the aged and very righteous king of Kekaya, father-in-law of this lion among kings, with his son.
ramayana-1-12-21.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-22.translation: 'Bring with honour the fortunate Lomapada, lord of Anga, the famous friend of this lion among kings.
ramayana-1-12-22.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-23.translation: 'Bring all the kings of the east, of Sindhu-Sauvira, of Saurashtra, and of the south.
ramayana-1-12-23.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-24.translation: 'And quickly bring the other friendly kings on earth, with their followers and kin.'
ramayana-1-12-24.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-25.translation: Hearing Vasishtha, Sumantra quickly sent good men to bring the kings.
ramayana-1-12-25.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-26.translation: At the sage's command, the righteous Sumantra himself hurried off to bring the kings.
ramayana-1-12-26.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-27.translation: All the overseers reported to wise Vasishtha everything prepared for the sacrifice.
ramayana-1-12-27.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-28.translation: Pleased, the best of Brahmins told them again: 'Nothing should be given to anyone with disrespect or carelessly. What is given with contempt destroys the giver, without doubt.'
ramayana-1-12-28.meaning: Giving without respect harms the giver.
ramayana-1-12-28.explanation: A lasting lesson: the spirit in which we give matters as much as the gift.

ramayana-1-12-29.translation: Within a few days the kings arrived, bringing many jewels for King Dasharatha.
ramayana-1-12-29.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-30.translation: Then Vasishtha, well pleased, said to the king: 'Tiger among men, the kings have come at your command.
ramayana-1-12-30.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-31.translation: 'I have honoured them all as they deserve, and the sacrificial preparations have been made by careful men.
ramayana-1-12-31.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-32.translation: 'Go out to sacrifice at the nearby sacrificial ground, which is supplied on all sides with every desired thing.'
ramayana-1-12-32.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-33.translation: At the word of Vasishtha and Rishyashringa, the king set out on an auspicious day under a good star.
ramayana-1-12-33.meaning: The king set out on an auspicious day.
ramayana-1-12-33.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.

ramayana-1-12-34.translation: Then all the best Brahmins, led by Vasishtha and with Rishyashringa in front, began the sacrifice.
ramayana-1-12-34.explanation: Bala Kanda, chapter 12: Vasishtha organizes the great sacrifice and invites kings from everywhere.
